l: the Gardens of delight, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The Gardens of delight are promised to single-minded slaves of Allah. They contain honor, couches facing one another, a gushing spring, pure drink, fruits, and companions of modest gaze and lovely eyes.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The Day of Judgment arrives with one Shout, after which people behold their condition and regret what they denied. The guilty are assembled, questioned, and requited for what they did.

l: the Day of Separation, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The Day of Separation is identified as the day the people used to deny. On it, those who did wrong are assembled with their wives and what they worshiped and are led toward hell.

l: the Resurrection, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The text teaches that the dead will be raised after becoming dust and bones. The deniers are told that they will be brought low and will come to know the truth.

l: the sacrifice of Abraham's son, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Abraham saw in a dream that he must sacrifice his son and told him of the command. After both surrendered, Allah declared that the vision had been fulfilled and ransomed the son with a tremendous victim.

l: the Doom, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The Doom is tasted by those who deny the truth, worship beside Allah, and follow error. The guilty share in it, while single-minded slaves of Allah are saved from it.

l: creation, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Allah created people from plastic clay and created them and what they make. The unit asks whether the deniers are stronger as a creation or those others Allah created.

l: revelation and remembrance, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The Word is read for a reminder, and warners are sent among peoples. Those who reject the reminder disbelieve in it, although they will come to know its truth.

l: the tree of Zaqqum, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The tree of Zaqqum is appointed as a torment for wrong-doers and springs from the heart of hell. Its crop is described as resembling the heads of devils, and the guilty must eat from it before drinking boiling water.

l: guidance, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Allah guides those who turn to Him, as shown when Abraham said he was going to his Lord who would guide him. Allah also showed Moses and Aaron the right path.

l: worship, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The unit condemns worship of carved gods and calls people to worship Allah, the Best of creators. Abraham asks his father and people what they worship and challenges their worship of false gods beside Allah.

l: monotheism, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Monotheism is stated in the declaration that there is no Allah save Allah. The idolaters scorned this declaration, but the unit confirms Allah's oneness and rejects all claims that He has offspring or partners.

l: judgment and accountability, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: People are assembled, stopped, and questioned about their conduct and worship. They are requited only for what they did, and the guilty mutually question and accuse one another before sharing the doom.

l: punishment, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Punishment includes perpetual torment, the painful doom, hell, the tree of Zaqqum, and boiling water. It is assigned to wrong-doers, deniers, and those who worship beside Allah.

l: salvation and reward, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Allah saves His believing slaves and rewards the good with provision, fruits, honor, peace, and the Gardens of delight. Noah, Abraham, his son, Moses, Aaron, Elias, Lot, and Jonah are presented in accounts involving Allah's saving favor or deliverance.

This unit concerns Allah’s revelation to Muhammad, the Arabic Lecture, and the call to establish religion without division. It describes Allah’s sovereignty, mercy, judgment, provision, signs in creation, and guidance to the path of Allah. Believers are characterized by faith, good works, worship, counsel, spending, patience, forgiveness, and defending themselves against wrongdoing. Wrong-doers and disbelievers face loss, punishment, and the doom, while the Garden is promised to those who believe and do good works.

Allah is the Creator, Sovereign, Protecting Friend, Forgiver, Merciful, Knower, Strong, Mighty, and Able to do all things. He reveals Scripture and guidance, accepts repentance, forgives evil deeds, provides for His slaves, sends rain, judges disputes, and brings people together for judgment.

Muhammad receives Allah’s inspiration and the Lecture in Arabic. He is commanded to warn mankind, summon them to religion, be upright, follow neither their lusts nor their arguments, and convey the message without being their warder.

Believers fear the Hour, trust in their Lord, shun the worst sins and indecencies, forgive when wroth, answer Allah’s call, establish worship, conduct their affairs by counsel, spend from what they have been given, and defend themselves after suffering wrong. They are promised flowering meadows of the Gardens and the better, lasting provision of Allah.

Wrong-doers have no friend or helper, and they face painful or awful doom. They are described as fearful of what they have earned, exposed to the Fire, humbled by disgrace, and without a road or refuge when Allah sends them astray.

Mankind is warned of the Day of assembling and urged to answer the call of the Lord before a day from Allah that cannot be averted. Man exults when he tastes mercy but is ungrateful when evil strikes him because of what his own hands have sent before.
The heavens belong to Allah, who created them and holds their keys. They almost rend asunder while the angels hymn the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth.
The earth belongs to Allah, who created it and whatever beasts He dispersed in it. It is also the place where people cannot escape Allah and where wrong-doers wrongfully rebel.
The Garden contains a host of people and flowering meadows for those who believe and do good works. Its people have what they wish from their Lord.
A host of people will be in the Flame. Those who disbelieve and those who reject the truth face an awful doom associated with it.

The Hereafter is the object of a harvest that Allah increases for those who desire it. It is better and more lasting than the passing comfort of the world, while those who desire only the world have no portion in the Hereafter.
The world provides only a passing comfort. Those who desire its harvest receive something of it, but they have no portion in the Hereafter.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 42: Consultation (Ash-Shura)
s: The Day of Resurrection is the day on which the eternal losers lose themselves and their housefolk. The wrong-doers remain in perpetual torment on that day.
The Hour may be nigh. Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while believers fear it and know that it is the Truth.

Allah reveals the Scripture with truth and inspires Muhammad with what He inspired earlier messengers. Muhammad did not know what the Scripture was until Allah made it a light by which He guides whom He wills.

Allah inspires Muhammad with a Lecture in Arabic so that he may warn the mother-town and those around it and warn of the Day of assembling. The Lecture calls people toward Allah’s guidance and the right path.
Allah speaks to mortals through revelation, from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals what He wills by His leave. He inspires Muhammad with a Spirit of His command.
Allah ordained for people the religion commended to Noah and inspired or commended to Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. They are commanded to establish it and not be divided in it.
Allah’s mercy reaches whom He wills. He accepts repentance, pardons evil deeds, increases the reward of those who do good works, and sends saving rain after people have despaired.
Those who believe and trust in their Lord shun the worst of sins and indecencies. Allah knows what people do and forgives much.
Believers answer the call of their Lord and establish worship. Worship is presented as part of the qualities of those who receive what Allah has and what is better and more lasting.

The affairs of believers are a matter of counsel. Counsel is listed among their qualities together with answering the call of their Lord, establishing worship, and spending from what Allah has bestowed on them.
The doom awaits disbelievers, wrong-doers, and those who reject or dispute Allah’s revelations. It is described as awful or painful, and those exposed to it seek a way of return.

l: the path of Allah, Surah 42: Consultation (Ash-Shura)
s: Muhammad guides toward the right path, which is the path of Allah. The path belongs to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and all things reach Him at last.

Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf) concerns Allah's revelation, the rejection of prophets, and the consequences awaiting believers and rejecters. It recounts how Muhammad, Moses, and Jesus delivered Allah's guidance, while their opponents mocked or disputed it. The unit contrasts the temporary wealth of the life of the world with the Garden for the believers and hell for the guilty. It affirms Allah's power over creation, resurrection, judgment, and the Hour.

l: Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf), Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: It presents Allah's Arabic revelation as clear, sublime, and decisive. It describes rejection of prophets, worldly wealth as temporary, and the differing destinies of believers and the guilty.

Allah created the heavens and the earth, made the earth a resting-place, sent down water, created pairs, and subjected ships and cattle for people to ride. Allah sent prophets and revelations, apportioned livelihood, will judge people, and will return them to Himself.
Muhammad is told to hold fast to what is inspired in him because he is on a right path. He is told to ask previous messengers, bear with rejecters, and say peace while they will come to know.
Moses was sent with Allah's revelations to Pharaoh and his chiefs. They laughed at his signs, promised to follow guidance when torment was removed, then broke their word.

Jesus, the son of Mary, is described as a slave upon whom Allah bestowed favour and as a pattern for the Children of Israel. He came with clear proofs and wisdom, called people to duty to Allah and obedience, and declared Allah to be his Lord and theirs.
Pharaoh proclaimed his sovereignty over Egypt and its rivers and claimed superiority over Moses. He persuaded his people to make light of Moses, and they obeyed him.

l: the earth, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: Allah made the earth a resting-place and placed roads in it. Allah revives dead land with water, and the earth is among what He created and rules.

l: the Garden, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The Garden is inherited by those who believed Allah's revelations and surrendered themselves. It contains gold trays, goblets, desired things, and abundant fruit, and its people remain immortal.
The guilty are immortal in hell's torment. Its torment is not relaxed, and they despair there.

l: the Hour, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The Hour has knowledge associated with Allah and will come suddenly. People are told not to doubt it, and they will be returned to Allah.
Allah's revelations were sent through Moses and were brought as clear proofs. Those who believe in them enter the Garden, while those who reject the Truth face punishment.
Many prophets were sent among earlier peoples, but their people mocked them. Earlier messengers were asked whether Allah appointed gods beside the Beneficent.

l: the folk, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The folk repeatedly rejected messengers, followed the religion of their fathers, and disputed the Truth. The folk of Pharaoh obeyed Pharaoh and were drowned after angering Allah.

l: the fathers, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: People claimed that their fathers followed a religion and used their footprints as guidance. This inherited practice was challenged when a warner brought better guidance.

l: the Children of Israel, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: Jesus was made a pattern for the Children of Israel. They are mentioned in connection with the favour bestowed upon him.

l: the angels, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The angels are described as slaves of the Beneficent, though people falsely called them females. Their creation was not witnessed by those who made this claim, and they will be questioned about their testimony.
Satan is an open enemy who turns people aside from the right path. People are warned not to let him divert them.
A devil is assigned as a comrade to whoever is dim to the remembrance of the Beneficent. Such companions turn people from Allah's way while they think they are rightly guided.

l: the believers, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The believers are those who believed Allah's revelations and surrendered themselves. They are told to enter the Garden without fear or grief.

l: the guilty, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The guilty remain immortal in hell's torment and despair there. They are told that they wronged themselves and must remain.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The disbelievers reject the Truth and call it magic. The text says that roofs, stairs, doors, couches, and ornaments of gold could have been given to them, but such wealth would only be provision of the life of the world.
Gold is mentioned as a possible worldly adornment, including roofs, stairs, doors, couches, and ornaments. Gold trays and goblets are also found in the Garden.
People claimed to follow the religion of their fathers. The unit contrasts this inherited claim with the guidance brought by messengers.
Guidance comes through Allah's revelations and the messengers. Rejecters preferred the practices of their fathers, while Muhammad is told that he is on a right path.

l: the torment, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: Allah seized earlier rejecters with torment so that they might turn again. Pharaoh's people asked Moses for relief, but after it was removed they broke their word.

l: the drowning of Pharaoh's people, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: When Pharaoh's people angered Allah, He punished them and drowned them every one. They were made a thing past and an example for those after them.
Allah is said to have created the heavens, the earth, all pairs, and the people who question these matters. The text rejects assigning daughters or a son to Allah.
The revival of dead land is presented as an example of how people will be brought forth. People will return to Allah after the Hour.

People are criticized for worshipping others beside Allah and for claiming that Allah willed their worship of them. Jesus called people to worship Allah, and Abraham declared himself innocent of what his people worshipped.

l: the life of the world, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The life of the world includes apportioned livelihood, social rank, wealth, and gold adornments. These possessions are described as temporary provision, while the Hereafter with Allah is better for those who keep from evil.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 43: Ornaments of gold (Az-Zukhruf)
s: The Hereafter with Allah is for those who keep from evil. In it, believers receive the Garden, while the guilty remain in hell's torment.

Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya) concerns Allah's revelations, the portents in creation, and the responses of believers and disbelievers. It describes Allah's guidance, the clear road of Allah's commandment, and the signs in the heavens, the earth, and the sea. It warns disbelievers of hell and the Fire, and describes the Day of Resurrection when the nations are summoned and judged according to their deeds. It also teaches that the life of the world is temporary and that believers will receive mercy.
Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya) presents Allah's revelations, signs, guidance, judgments, and promises concerning believers and disbelievers.

Allah is the Mighty and the Wise, the source of revelation, guidance, mercy, provision, and judgment. Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, made what is in them serviceable, and will repay every soul for what it earned.
The believers recognize the portents of Allah and believe in the revelations. Those who believe and do good works will be brought into Allah's mercy.
The disbelievers reject or mock the revelations, follow falsehood, and deny the Hour. They will face a painful doom and the Fire.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya)
s: The revelations of Allah are recited with truth and provide guidance and clear indication. Some hear them with pride, make them a jest, or become scornful, and are warned of punishment.

l: the portents of Allah, Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya)
s: The portents of Allah appear in the heavens, the earth, human creation, beasts, night and day, provision from the sky, and the ordering of the winds. They are signs for believers and for people who have sense or reflect.
The heavens contain portents for believers and belong to Allah. Allah created the heavens with truth, and His Majesty belongs in them.
The earth contains portents, is quickened after its death by provision from the sky, and belongs to Allah. Allah created it with truth and made what is in it serviceable.

l: the clear road of Allah's commandment, Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya)
s: The clear road of Allah's commandment is set for Muhammad to follow. He is told to follow it and not the whims of those who know not.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya)
s: The Day of Resurrection is a certain day when Allah gathers mankind, judges their differences, and repays them for what they did. The nations are summoned to their record on that day.
The Hour is promised by Allah and its coming has no doubt. Disbelievers call it a conjecture, but they will be judged when it rises.
Hell awaits those beyond the truth, and what they earned or chose as protecting friends beside Allah will not avail them. It is described as an awful doom.
The Fire is the habitation of those who forgot the meeting of the Day of Resurrection and treated Allah's revelations as a jest. They will not come forth from it or make amends.

l: the life of the world, Surah 45: Crouching (Al-Jaathiya)
s: The life of the world beguiles disbelievers, who claim that only worldly life exists and that time destroys them. Their attachment to it is condemned when they face judgment.
Allah's Book pronounces against people with truth and records all that they did. It is presented as the record by which they are requited.
The nations will be seen crouching and each nation will be summoned to its record. They will be told that they are requited for what they used to do.
Guidance is identified with Allah's clear indication and the revelations of the Lord. It is for a folk whose faith is sure.
Mercy belongs to Allah, and those who believe and do good works will be brought into it. It is described as part of the evident triumph.

The unit concerns Allah's signs, judgment, worship, and the fate of those who believe or disbelieve. It recounts Abraham's honoured guests, Moses and Pharaoh, A'ad, Thamud, and Noah, describing signs and punishments connected with them. It teaches that jinn and humankind were created to worship Allah, that all things were created in pairs, and that warning benefits believers. It promises gardens and watersprings for those who keep from evil and an evil day for disbelievers and wrongdoers.

Allah is described as the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the giver of livelihood, and the possessor of unbreakable might. Jinn and humankind were created to worship Allah, and people are commanded not to set up another god along with Allah.
Muhammad is addressed as the one who receives the story of Abraham's honoured guests. He is told to withdraw from those who reject him, to warn, and that he is not blameworthy.

Abraham received honoured guests whom he did not know, brought them a fatted calf, and offered it to them. He feared them until they reassured him and gave him tidings of a wise son, and he asked about their errand.

l: Abraham's honoured guests, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: Abraham's honoured guests came to him, greeted him, and were given a fatted calf. They reassured him, announced a wise son, and said they had been sent to a guilty folk to send marked stones of clay upon them.
Moses was sent to Pharaoh with clear warrant. Pharaoh withdrew in his might and called him a wizard or a madman, so Allah seized Pharaoh and his hosts and flung them into the sea.
Pharaoh received Moses with clear warrant but withdrew in his might and called him a wizard or a madman. Allah seized Pharaoh and his hosts and flung them into the sea, and Pharaoh was reprobate.
A'ad had a sign in the fatal wind that was sent against them. The wind spared nothing it reached and made it as dust.
Thamud were told to take their ease awhile, but they rebelled against their Lord's decree. The thunderbolt overtook them while they gazed, and they were unable to rise up or help themselves.
The folk of Noah are mentioned as having been licentious folk.
The jinn were created by Allah only so that they might worship Him. Allah does not seek livelihood from them or ask them to feed Him.
Humankind were created by Allah only so that they might worship Him. Allah does not seek livelihood from them or ask them to feed Him.

Believers are told that warning benefits them. Those who keep from evil will dwell amid gardens and watersprings, and one house of those surrendered to Allah was found among the people brought forth from the punished folk.
Disbelievers are promised woe on the day they are promised. Their day is described as an evil day like the evil day that came for their likes of old.

l: guilty folk, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: The honoured guests said they were sent to a guilty folk to send marked stones of clay upon them. The stones were marked by Allah for the destruction of the wanton.

Messengers came to those before the people addressed in the unit, but the people called each messenger a wizard or a madman. The text says that this response was not handed down as an heirloom, but that those people were froward.
Heaven is described as full of paths, built with might, and made vast in extent. Providence and what is promised are said to be in heaven.
The earth contains portents for those whose faith is sure. It was laid out by Allah, described as graciously spread, and presented as a sign alongside the heavens.
Gardens and watersprings are the dwelling place promised to those who keep from evil. They receive what their Lord gives them because they were formerly doers of good.
The Fire is where those who ask when the Day of Judgment will be are tormented. They are told to taste the torment they sought to hasten.

l: Day of Judgment, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: The Day of Judgment is asked about by those who are careless in an abyss. It is described as the day when they will be tormented at the Fire and as the day promised to disbelievers.

l: fatal wind against A'ad, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: The fatal wind was sent against A'ad. It spared nothing that it reached and made it as dust.

l: thunderbolt overtaking Thamud, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: The thunderbolt overtook Thamud while they gazed after they rebelled against their Lord's decree. They could neither rise up nor help themselves.

l: creation in pairs, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: Allah created all things in pairs so that people might reflect.

l: worship of Allah, Surah 51: The Winnowing Winds (Adh-Dhaariyat)
s: Worship of Allah is the purpose for which Allah created the jinn and humankind. They are commanded to flee unto Allah and not set any other god along with Him.
Warning is presented as a duty and as something that benefits believers. Muhammad is told to warn, and he is described as a plain warner from Allah.

The Beneficent has made known the Qur'an, created man and jinn, taught man utterance, and established the ordered heavens, earth, seas, and other signs. Man and jinn are reminded repeatedly of the favours of their Lord and are told they cannot escape His authority. The guilty will be recognized, punished in hell, and made to circle between fire and boiling water. Those who fear standing before their Lord are promised two gardens and two other gardens with fountains, fruits, beautiful companions, and places of rest.

The Beneficent has made known the Qur'an, created man and jinn, taught man utterance, and established the measure in the heavens and earth. He is Lord of the two Easts and two Wests, and all in the heavens and earth entreat Him; every day He exercises universal power.
The Qur'an is made known by the Beneficent.

Man was created from clay like the potter's and was taught utterance. Man and jinn are told that they cannot penetrate the regions of the heavens and earth without sanction, and on the Day neither man nor jinni will be questioned of his sin.

The jinn were created from smokeless fire. Jinn and men are addressed together as dependents and are told they cannot escape the regions of the heavens and earth without sanction; the guilty among them will be identified and punished.
The earth was appointed for the Beneficent's creatures. It contains fruit, sheathed palm-trees, husked grain, and scented herb.
The heavens are uplifted with the measure set by the Beneficent. The sun and moon are made punctual, and the stars prostrate; the regions of the heavens cannot be penetrated without sanction.
The guilty will be known by their marks and taken by the forelocks and feet. They will enter hell and circle between it and fierce, boiling water.
Hell is presented as the place which the guilty deny. The guilty circle between hell and fierce, boiling water.

For whoever fears standing before his Lord there are two gardens. They have spreading branches, two flowing fountains, every kind of fruit in pairs, silk-brocade-lined couches, and fruit near to hand; they also contain modest-gazed companions untouched before them, like jacynth and coral-stone.

l: favours of your Lord, Surah 55: The Beneficent (Ar-Rahmaan)
s: The text repeatedly asks which of the favours of the Lord man and jinn will deny. These favours include creation, ordered natural signs, the earth's provisions, ships, the promise of gardens, fruits, fountains, companions, and rest.

The unit concerns the Sovereignty (Al-Mulk), declaring Allah’s power over creation, life, death, the heavens, the earth, provision, and resurrection. It describes the fate of the disbelievers in hell, where they acknowledge that they denied the warnings. Muhammad is instructed to warn people, affirm trust in Allah, and answer questions about judgment, protection, and provision. The unit urges people to observe creation, give thanks, and recognize that knowledge and sustenance belong to Allah.
The Sovereignty (Al-Mulk) is the subject of a unit revealed at Mecca. It declares that blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty and that He is Able to do all things.

Allah is described as the Creator of life, death, the heavens, the earth, and human faculties. He is the Mighty, the Forgiving, the Beneficent, the Subtile, and the Aware; He knows what is in the breasts, provides sustenance, and to Him people will be gathered.

Muhammad is instructed to warn people, say that knowledge belongs to Allah only, and declare belief and trust in the Beneficent. He is also instructed to ask who could protect the disbelievers from a painful doom or bring gushing water if their water disappeared into the earth.

Hell is the doom prepared for those who disbelieve in their Lord. When people are flung into it, they hear its roaring, its wardens question them about a warner, and its dwellers acknowledge their sins.
The disbelievers deny the warnings and say that Allah has revealed nothing. They are described as being in illusion, pride, and frowardness, and a painful doom awaits them.
The earth has been made subservient to people, who are told to walk in its paths and eat of Allah’s providence. It may swallow people when convulsed, and their water may disappear into it.
The resurrection of the dead is to Allah. People will be gathered unto Him after being multiplied in the earth.

The unit concerns Muhammad, whom Allah describes as not mad and as possessing a tremendous nature, with an unfailing reward promised to him. It warns Muhammad against obeying the rejecters and describes their slander, wrongdoing, and denial of Allah's revelations. It recounts how the owners of the garden lost its fruit after resolving to exclude the needy, then regretted their wrongdoing and hoped for better from their Lord. It contrasts those who keep from evil, who will have gardens of bliss, with the guilty, and warns of the punishment of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment.
Allah is described as Muhammad's Lord, Best Aware of those who stray and those who walk aright. Allah tries people, sends punishment, grants favor, chooses among them, and possesses a firm scheme.

Muhammad is told that he is not a madman, that he will have an unfailing reward, and that he possesses a tremendous nature. He is instructed not to obey the rejecters, to wait for his Lord's decree, and not to be like him of the fish.

The rejecters are described as wanting Muhammad to compromise so that they may compromise. They include feeble oath-mongers, detracters, spreaders of slanders, hinderers of good, transgressors, malefactors, and intrusive people.
The disbelievers would fain disconcert Muhammad with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say that he is mad. Their claim is contradicted because the Reminder is for creation.

l: the owners of the garden, Surah 68: The Pen (Al-Qalam)
s: The owners of the garden vowed to pluck its fruit the next morning without making an exception for Allah's will. After the garden was destroyed, they recognized their error, glorified their Lord, admitted wrongdoing, and hoped for something better in its place.
The garden was tested when a visitation from Muhammad's Lord came upon it while its owners slept. By morning it was as if its fruit had been plucked, and its owners found it desolate.
The Reminder is heard by the disbelievers, who respond by saying that Muhammad is mad. The unit states that it is nothing other than a Reminder to creation.
Allah's revelations are recited to a person who responds by calling them mere fables of the men of old. The unit says that this person will be branded on the nose.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 68: The Pen (Al-Qalam)
s: The Day of Judgment is presented as the day when those who claim to have a covenant from Allah will be tested regarding what they ordain. On that day, people will be ordered to prostrate themselves, but some will be unable to do so.
The punishment of the Hereafter is said to be greater than the punishment that befell the garden, if people only knew. Those who keep from evil are promised gardens of bliss with their Lord.

l: gardens of bliss, Surah 68: The Pen (Al-Qalam)
s: Gardens of bliss are promised to those who keep from evil with their Lord. They are contrasted with the treatment of the guilty.
The punishment is illustrated by the destruction of the garden after its owners resolved to exclude the needy. The unit says that the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.

l: the garden's destruction, Surah 68: The Pen (Al-Qalam)
s: The garden's destruction occurred while its owners slept, after they had vowed to pluck its fruit without making an exception for Allah's will. In the morning it appeared as if it had been plucked, leading its owners to recognize that they were wrongdoers.

The Reality concerns the judgment to come, the destruction of Thamud, A'ad, Pharaoh, and other communities, and the events that accompany the final Event. Allah describes the trumpet blast, the lifting and crushing of the earth and mountains, the splitting of the heaven, and the exposure of all people. Those given their record in the right hand enter bliss, while those given it in the left hand are fettered and cast into hell-fire. The unit declares that the revelation is the speech of an illustrious messenger from the Lord of the Worlds and absolute truth.
The Reality is proclaimed, and the text asks what it is and what will convey its nature. It is associated with the judgment to come and the final Event.
Thamud disbelieved in the judgment to come and were destroyed by the lightning.
A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come and were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days.
Allah is the Tremendous Lord whose name is to be glorified. He destroyed disobedient communities, causes the final events to occur, and will judge people according to their records.

l: the Lord of the Worlds, Surah 69: The Reality (Al-Haaqqa)
s: The Lord of the Worlds is identified as the source of the revelation, which is the speech of an illustrious messenger.

l: the judgment to come, Surah 69: The Reality (Al-Haaqqa)
s: Thamud and A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come. The unit describes its accompanying reckoning and final exposure of people.

l: the trumpet blast, Surah 69: The Reality (Al-Haaqqa)
s: The trumpet will sound one blast, after which the earth and mountains will be lifted and crushed and the Event will befall.
The earth will be lifted up together with the mountains and crushed with one crash.
The mountains will be lifted up with the earth and crushed with one crash.
The heaven will split asunder and become frail on the day of the Event.
The record is given to each person in the right hand or the left hand. The one given it in the right hand rejoices, while the one given it in the left hand wishes it had not been given to him.
The person given his record in the left hand is ordered to be taken, fettered, and exposed to hell-fire.

l: the speech of an illustrious messenger, Surah 69: The Reality (Al-Haaqqa)
s: The text declares that it is the speech of an illustrious messenger, not a poet's speech or a diviner's speech.
The revelation is from the Lord of the Worlds and is described as a warrant for those who ward off evil, an anguish for disbelievers, and absolute truth.

The person given his record in the right hand knew he would meet his reckoning and enters a blissful state. The person given his record in the left hand laments not knowing what his reckoning would be.

Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba) concerns the awful tidings about which the questioners disagree. It describes signs of the Lord’s power, including the earth, the high hills, human beings, the seven strong heavens, rain, grain, plants, and gardens. It warns of the Day of Decision, when the heavens open, the hills move, hell receives the rebellious, and the deeds of all are recorded. It contrasts the torment of those who denied with the reward of the duteous and warns the disbeliever of a doom at hand.

l: Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba), Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: It presents the awful tidings about which the questioners disagree and warns of the Day of Decision and a doom at hand.

l: the awful tidings, Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: They are the subject of the questioners’ disagreement, and the text says that those who disagree will come to know.
They question one another concerning the awful tidings.
It has been made an expanse.
They have been created in pairs, and their sleep has been appointed for repose.

l: the seven strong heavens, Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: They have been built above human beings.
Gardens of thick foliage are produced through abundant water, and gardens enclosed are part of the achievement prepared for the duteous.

l: the Day of Decision, Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: It is a fixed time when the trumpet is blown, people come in multitudes, the heaven opens as gates, and the hills move like a mirage.
They stand arrayed with the Spirit on the day when none speak except those whom the Beneficent allows and who speak right.
The Spirit stands arrayed with the angels on the day when none speak except those whom the Beneficent allows and who speak right.
It lurks in ambush as a home for the rebellious.
They will abide in hell for ages and taste neither coolness nor drink, except boiling water and a paralysing cold.
The rebellious did not look for a reckoning.
They were called false by the rebellious with strong denial.
Those who deny are told to taste what they earned, with no increase given to them except torment.
They have achievement consisting of enclosed gardens, vineyards, voluptuous women of equal age, and a full cup, with no vain discourse or lying.

l: voluptuous women of equal age, Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: They are among the rewards prepared for the duteous.
The Beneficent is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all between them. None can converse with Him unless He allows them, and He allows those who speak right.
The Lord is described as the source of requital and a gift in payment, and as the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all between them.

l: the True Day, Surah 78: The Announcement (An-Naba)
s: It is the day when the angels and the Spirit stand arrayed and speech occurs only by the Beneficent’s allowance.
The disbeliever will look at what his own hands have sent before and cry, wishing to be dust.
A doom at hand is warned of as a day when a man sees what his own hands have sent before.

An-Naazi'aat describes the resurrection, when the trumpet is sounded, hearts tremble, and people are awakened from their graves. It recounts how Moses was sent to Pharaoh, who rebelled, denied the sign, and proclaimed himself the highest lord, so Allah seized him as an example. The unit describes Allah's creation of heaven and earth and His provision of water, pasture, and hills. It contrasts the fate of those who rebel and prefer the life of the world with those who fear their Lord, and states that only Allah knows the term of the Hour.

l: An-Naazi'aat, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: An-Naazi'aat concerns the events surrounding the resurrection, the story of Moses and Pharaoh, Allah's creation of heaven and earth, and the differing fates of people.

l: angels, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: The angels are described as hastening and governing the event.

l: Allah, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Allah seizes Pharaoh and makes him an example for the afterlife and for the former. Allah builds heaven, raises its height, orders it, darkens its night, brings forth its morning, spreads the earth, produces its water and pasture, and makes fast the hills.

l: Moses, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Moses is called by his Lord in the holy vale of Tuwa and sent to Pharaoh, with guidance offered to him toward his Lord and fear of Him. Moses shows Pharaoh the tremendous token.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Pharaoh is described as having rebelled, denied the tremendous token, disobeyed, turned away, gathered and summoned, and proclaimed that he was the highest lord. Allah seizes Pharaoh as an example for the afterlife and for the former.

l: heaven, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Heaven is built by Allah, who raises its height and orders it, makes its night dark, and brings forth its morning.

l: earth, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Allah spreads the earth, produces its water and pasture, and makes fast the hills. These are described as a provision for people and their cattle.

l: great disaster, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: The great disaster comes on the day when man remembers his whole endeavour and hell stands visibly before him who sees.

l: hell, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: Hell stands forth visible at the great disaster. It is the home of those who rebel and choose the life of the world.

l: Garden, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: The Garden is the home of the person who fears standing before his Lord and restrains his soul from lust.

l: life of the world, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: The life of the world is chosen by those who rebel, and hell is their home.

l: Hour, Surah 79: Those who drag forth (An-Naazi'aat)
s: People ask when the Hour will come, but its term belongs to Allah. On the day they behold it, they will feel as though they had tarried only for an evening or its morning.

The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq) describes the heaven and earth responding attentively to Allah and the final accounting of man. Those given their account in their right hand receive an easy reckoning and return joyfully to their folk, while those given it behind their back face destruction and scorching fire. The text warns that all people journey from plane to plane and that Allah knows what those who disbelieve conceal. Those who believe and do good works receive an unfailing reward.

l: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq), Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq) concerns the splitting of the heaven, the spreading of the earth, and the accounting and destiny of man.
The heaven is split asunder and is attentive to Allah in fear.
The earth is spread out, casts out all that was in it, becomes empty, and is attentive to Allah in fear.
Allah is the Lord to whom the heaven, the earth, and man are directed. Allah is ever looking on man and knows best what those who disbelieve are hiding.
Man works toward his Lord a work that he will meet in His presence. Man is accounted according to what he is given, and he journeys from plane to plane.

l: the man’s account, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: The man’s account may be given in his right hand or behind his back. Receiving it in the right hand brings an easy reckoning, while receiving it behind the back leads to an invocation of destruction.

l: scorching fire, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: Those given their account behind their back are thrown to scorching fire.
When the Qur'an is recited to them, some do not worship Allah.

l: those who disbelieve, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: Those who disbelieve deny and conceal what they are doing. They are given tidings of a painful doom.

l: those who believe and do good works, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: Those who believe and do good works receive an unfailing reward.

l: painful doom, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: A painful doom is promised to those who disbelieve, except for those who believe and do good works.

l: unfailing reward, Surah 84: The Splitting Open (Al-Inshiqaaq)
s: An unfailing reward belongs to those who believe and do good works.

The unit describes the Overwhelming and what happens to people on that day. Many faces are downcast, toiling, weary, scorched by fire, drinking boiling water, and given only bitter thorn-fruit. Other faces are calm and glad for their past effort, dwelling in a high Garden with springs, couches, goblets, cushions, and silken carpets. The addressed figure is told to remind them, while Allah will punish those who are averse and disbelieve, and all will return to Him for reckoning.

l: Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya), Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: It describes the Overwhelming, the states of faces on that day, signs for reflection, the duty of the addressed figure, and the punishment, return, and reckoning ordained by Allah.

l: thee/thou (the addressed prophet), Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: The addressed figure is told to remind them and is described as a remembrancer, not a warder over them.

l: the day of judgment, Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: On that day, many faces will be downcast, toiling, weary, and scorched by burning fire, while other faces will be calm and glad for their effort past.

l: the punished people, Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: They have downcast faces, toil and weariness, and are scorched by burning fire. They drink from a boiling spring and receive no food except bitter thorn-fruit that neither nourishes nor releases them from hunger.

l: the blessed people, Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: Their faces are calm and they are glad for their effort past. They are in a high Garden with no idle speech, a gushing spring, raised couches, goblets set at hand, ranged cushions, and spread silken carpets.

l: the high Garden, Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: It is a place where the blessed people hear no idle speech and where there are a gushing spring, raised couches, goblets set at hand, ranged cushions, and spread silken carpets.
Allah will punish whoever is averse and disbelieves with direst punishment. The return of those people is to Allah, and their reckoning belongs to Him.
It is the punishment Allah will give to whoever is averse and disbelieves.

l: the return to Allah, Surah 88: The Overwhelming (Al-Ghaashiya)
s: The text says that the return of the people is unto Allah.
The text says that the reckoning belongs to Allah.

Surah 89: The Dawn concerns the oath of the Dawn, ten nights, the Even and the Odd, and the departing night. It recounts how the Lord dealt with A'ad, Iram, Thamud, and Pharaoh because of their rebellion and iniquity. It describes man's mistaken judgments about honor and deprivation, and his failure to honor the orphan or feed the poor. It warns of the Day when the earth is ground to atoms, the angels come rank on rank, hell is brought near, and the soul at peace is invited to return to its Lord and enter the Garden.

l: Surah 89: The Dawn (Al-Fajr), Surah 89: The Dawn (Al-Fajr)
s: Surah 89: The Dawn is revealed at Mecca and concerns oaths, past rebellious peoples, man's conduct, punishment, and the final return to the Lord.
Allah is referenced in connection with the rebellious peoples' disobedience and with the punishment that the Lord brings upon them.
A'ad is described as a people dealt with by the Lord after their rebellion and iniquity in the lands.
Iram is described as having many columns and as unlike anything created in the lands.
Thamud is described as a people who clove the rocks in the valley and were dealt with by the Lord after their rebellion and iniquity.
Pharaoh is described as firm of might and as among those who were rebellious and multiplied iniquity in the lands.

Man says that his Lord honors him when he is tried through honor and ease, but says that his Lord despises him when his means of life are straitened. Man is reproached for not honoring the orphan, not urging the feeding of the poor, devouring heritages with greed, and loving wealth with abounding love. On the day when hell is brought near, man remembers and wishes he had sent provision before him for his life.
The earth is described as being ground to atoms, grinding, grinding, before the Lord comes with angels rank on rank.
The angels come rank on rank when the Lord comes on the final day.
Hell is brought near on that day, when man remembers but finds that remembrance of no avail.

l: soul at peace, Surah 89: The Dawn (Al-Fajr)
s: The soul at peace is called to return to its Lord, content in His good pleasure, and to enter among His bondmen.
The Garden is the destination into which the soul at peace is commanded to enter.

The unit concerns the sun, moon, day, night, heaven, earth, and soul as signs of creation. It teaches that the soul is successful when caused to grow and fails when stunted. It recounts how (The tribe of) Thamud denied the truth, and how the basest of them hamstrung the she-camel of Allah after the messenger of Allah told them to let her drink. Allah doomed them for their sin and razed their dwellings.
The Sun is mentioned with its brightness.
Allah is described as the One Who built the heaven, spread the earth, and perfected the soul. Allah doomed (The tribe of) Thamud for their sin and razed their dwellings.
The soul is perfected and inspired with conscience of what is wrong and right for it. It is successful when caused to grow and fails when stunted.

l: (The tribe of) Thamud, Surah 91: The Sun (Ash-Shams)
s: (The tribe of) Thamud denied the truth in rebellious pride. After the basest of them broke forth and the she-camel of Allah was hamstrung, Allah doomed them for their sin and razed their dwellings.

l: the basest of them, Surah 91: The Sun (Ash-Shams)
s: The basest of them broke forth and hamstrung the she-camel of Allah after the messenger of Allah told them to let her drink.

l: messenger of Allah, Surah 91: The Sun (Ash-Shams)
s: The messenger of Allah said that the she-camel of Allah should be allowed to drink.

l: she-camel of Allah, Surah 91: The Sun (Ash-Shams)
s: The she-camel of Allah was to be allowed to drink. (The tribe of) Thamud denied the messenger of Allah and hamstrung her.

Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa) concerns the Lord’s reassurance and guidance to the addressed person. It says that the Lord has not forsaken or hated the addressed person and that the latter portion will be better than the former. The Lord promises to give to the addressed person until the addressed person is content, recalling that He protected, directed, and enriched the addressed person. The unit commands that the orphan not be oppressed, the beggar not be driven away, and the bounty of the Lord be spoken of.

l: Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa), Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa)
s: It presents assurances from the Lord to the addressed person and commands proper treatment of the orphan and beggar, along with discourse about the bounty of the Lord.

l: the addressed person, Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa)
s: The addressed person has not been forsaken or hated by the Lord. The Lord found the addressed person an orphan and protected the addressed person, found the addressed person wandering and directed the addressed person, and found the addressed person destitute and enriched the addressed person.

l: the Lord, Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa)
s: The Lord has not forsaken or hated the addressed person. He promises that the latter portion will be better than the former and that He will give to the addressed person until the addressed person is content; He also protected, directed, and enriched the addressed person.
The orphan is not to be oppressed.
The beggar is not to be driven away.

l: bounty of the Lord, Surah 93: The Morning Hours (Ad-Dhuhaa)
s: The bounty of the Lord is to be spoken of.

Surah 94: The Consolation (Ash-Sharh), revealed at Mecca, speaks to one whose bosom has been dilated and burden eased. It says that hardship is accompanied by ease, repeating this assurance twice. When relieved, the addressed person is told to continue toiling and strive to please the Lord.

l: Surah 94: The Consolation (Ash-Sharh), Surah 94: The Consolation (Ash-Sharh)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and presents reassurance that hardship is accompanied by ease. It instructs the addressed person to continue toiling when relieved and to strive to please the Lord.

l: deity (the speaker and Lord), Surah 94: The Consolation (Ash-Sharh)
s: The deity is presented as having caused the addressed person's bosom to dilate, eased the burden weighing down the back, and exalted the person's fame. The deity is also identified as the Lord whom the person should strive to please.
